questions.cardText:
[Political Science] Which of the following is a “banana republic”?
A. A tropical country with a monarchy
B. A politically unstable country
C. A republic where bananas are the primary food source
Answer: B. The term “banana republic” was coined to describe countries like Honduras, where political instability was intertwined with economic dependence on banana exports. However, this term has been eschewed by many scholars today due to its potential derogatory connotations.
questions.de: Welcher Begriff, von O. Henry mit Blick auf Honduras geprägt, bezeichnet ein politisch instabiles Land, dessen Wirtschaft vom Export eines einzigen Rohstoffs abhängt?
questions.en: What term, coined by O. Henry with Honduras in mind, describes a politically unstable country whose economy depends on exporting a single resource?

timeline.labelEn: O. Henry coins ‘banana republic’ in his book Cabbages and Kings
timeline.labelDe: O. Henry prägt in seinem Buch „Cabbages and Kings“ den Begriff „Bananenrepublik“

questions.notes: Reversed into a term question (the card's 'which is' only works among the options). Wikipedia: coined by O. Henry in 1904, inspired by his time in Honduras.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which mammal is known for its ability to delay pregnancy?
A. Kangaroo B. Elephant C. Dolphin
Answer: A. Kangaroos have the unique ability to delay the development of their embryo until environmental conditions are favorable.
questions.de: Wie heißt die Fähigkeit von Kängurus, die Entwicklung eines befruchteten Embryos anzuhalten, bis die Bedingungen günstig sind?
questions.en: What is the name for the ability of kangaroos to halt the development of a fertilised embryo until conditions are favourable?

timeline.labelEn: Joseph Banks first records the name ‘kanguru’ in his diary at the Endeavour River
timeline.labelDe: Joseph Banks hält am Endeavour River erstmals den Namen „kanguru“ in seinem Tagebuch fest

questions.notes: Card error: the ability is not unique to kangaroos — Wikipedia (Embryonic diapause) lists over 130 mammals incl. bears, rodents, mustelids and the roe deer. The question therefore asks the name of the phenomenon.
